_provenance.purpose: Development set for the Laya answerability gate (src/decisions/answerability.py). Instruction phrasing and thresholds are chosen on THIS set only; tests/golden_qa_set.json (35 answerable + 6 controls) is held out as the test set. Written by hand for the Aurora sample deal (data/sample_deal/*.txt), 2026-09-24, with wording deliberately different from the golden set.
_provenance.design: Mostly minimal pairs: an unanswerable question asks for a figure or fact adjacent to one the corpus does state (a different year, party, metric or granularity), so retrieval returns on-topic passages with high reranker scores - exactly the case the reranker-score heuristic cannot refuse. `pair` links an unanswerable entry to its answerable twin.
_provenance.verification: Answerable entries carry `evidence`: a verbatim corpus excerpt (whitespace-normalised) in `source`. Unanswerable entries carry `absence_patterns`: case-insensitive regexes that match NOWHERE in the corpus, plus `absent` naming what is missing. tests/test_decisions_query.py::test_answerability_dev_set_is_verified re-checks both against data/sample_deal on every CI run, so an edit to the corpus that makes an unanswerable question answerable fails loudly.
_provenance.caveat: Absence is verified by pattern, not by a human reading every sentence. Where an unanswerable question has a near-answer in the corpus (e.g. a settlement range but no agreed settlement) that is noted in `absent`; those are the hard cases the gate must not be flattered on.
